changes.ink: The rounded group glyph repeats the extension letter. Ens ends before the insertion leader without a period or an extra comma. The ne-empty-set condition is above the line and attaches after ens; the baseline comma follows the insertion position.
The pi is unindexed here. It is followed by the open-right inclusion sign and the same rounded unprimed group glyph. E/Sigma remains uncertain under the common notation.
The first category C stands at the right of its line with blank paper immediately after it. No separate terminal dot is visible; the later C-prime sentence, by contrast, has an explicit dark period.

The fourth component is a large rounded capital with a long looped descender, matching cal G in the extension. H explicitly renders this source form as ordinary G; the candidate preserves C’s calligraphic rendering.

The final small letter has a closed upper oval and a distinct descending hooked loop below its body, ending near the tuple commas. This is the g form. It differs visibly from the low non-descending action label before the later colon.

After the closing parenthesis there is a small o trace, a separate low u stroke and a short accent above the latter. These are three horizontally arranged components, rather than a vertical colon pair.
The group letter has the recurrent rounded upper bowl and long descending stem, with no prime. Its calligraphic encoding is retained consistently.

One word between opérant and the live sur is crossed by a long horizontal stroke. A small upper loop, a lower leftward return and low following strokes survive. They allow sur or de but do not securely establish either; the uncertain reading is retained rather than presented as a recovered certain word.

The letter immediately before the colon is a low short a-shaped stroke without a descender, unlike the final g in the tuple. The following group has the large round descending cal G form. The map has a clearly pointed right arrowhead, and the target is Aut(Pi). The tuple/map label discrepancy is preserved.
The lower-left pencil number has a thin slanted 1 and a 6 with a closed lower loop, reading 16.

notes.text: The page begins by saying that the envisaged arrow follows immediately. It then explicitly asks to explain how (7) and (8) result from the action on the covered set, whose fundamental-group subgroup acts freely with J as “ens quotient”. The wording “Il faudrait encore expliciter comment (7) (8) résultent” is a request for an explanation, not a proof supplied on this page.

The reformulation considers a group extension together with a nonempty set on which the extension group acts and the kernel acts freely; these systems form the category C. It then considers a connected groupoid with a universal cover and a group action, declaring a category C-prime. A small addition beside connexe remains unreadable between the supplied nonempty alternatives and is not completed from the intended mathematics.

The source announces equivalences that will be defined, quasi-inverse to one another: alpha goes from C to C-prime and beta returns from C-prime to C. No construction of these functors or proof of equivalence appears here. The tuple ends in a descending g, while the later action homomorphism is labelled with a low a; the discrepancy is preserved rather than harmonized.

Four bare shafts in the extension and the absence of a period after the first category C are preserved. The upper paragraph ends in four points. The later action homomorphism and the two bottom functor arrows do have visible arrowheads.

raw_difference_disposition: All 29 raw packet differences were inspected against the original and both native-resolution halves, with all words, symbols, underlines, corrections and punctuation also read where the witnesses agree. Material differences are covered above; a single extension-diagram row covers the four connectors and its group symbols as one expression. Pure macro syntax, braces, wrappers, arrow-rendering syntax for the equivalent final diagram, and H’s editorial note about rendering G were excluded. Only original packet mark M0690 appears in decisions. New/common doubts are recorded in remaining_doubts. The original and each half were viewed once; eight unique crops were made once each from the original. No other page or packet was inspected, and no web, OCR or TeX compilation was used.

main_adjudication.summary: Original page and all eight reader crops plus four main crops inspected. Candidate retained, with evidence mapping and confidence corrected. The tuple g and later low a are both preserved; M0690 and crossed word remain uncertain.
